title: Cross-Team Data Flow and Report Consolidation
purpose: Defines how data flows between teams within and across simultaneous projects. Covers report formats, consolidation pipelines, deduplication, and final output assembly.

section_1_report_standardization.title: Standard Report Formats
section_1_report_standardization.description: All team outputs must follow standardized formats for automated consolidation.

required_metadata_block.description: Every output JSON file MUST start with this metadata block.

bug_report.aggregation_strategy: Merge bug arrays, deduplicate by id, take highest severity when duplicated

documentation_report.aggregation_strategy: Merge gap arrays, merge documentation sections by key

assessment_report.aggregation_strategy: Merge test results, deduplicate fixed bugs

section_2_consolidation_pipeline.title: Report Consolidation Pipeline
section_2_consolidation_pipeline.description: Step-by-step process for merging outputs from all teams into final deliverables.

pipeline_steps.name: Validate
pipeline_steps.action: Verify each file is valid JSON with required metadata block

pipeline_steps.name: Categorize
pipeline_steps.action: Group reports by type (index, bug, documentation, assessment)
pipeline_steps.method: Read metadata.task field to determine report type

pipeline_steps.name: Deduplicate
pipeline_steps.action: Within each category, remove duplicate findings across teams
rules: Bug reports: match by file + line + description similarity. Keep the version with more detail.
Index entries: match by file path. Merge metadata from multiple teams.
Tool assessments: match by tool name. Keep the most recent test result.
Documentation: merge by section key. Combine content from multiple teams.

pipeline_steps.name: Cross-reference
examples: Bug in tool X (bug report) → Tool X marked broken (assessment report)
Missing docs for module Y (documentation report) → Module Y index entry updated
Fixed bug in Z (bug report) → Z re-tested and verified (assessment report)

rules.rule: Teams within the same project group MAY read each other's outputs
rules.rationale: Same-project teams benefit from shared findings without coordination overhead

rules.rule: Teams across project groups should NOT depend on each other's outputs
rules.rationale: Cross-project dependencies create sequencing. Keep projects independent.

rules.rule: All teams MAY read prior session outputs (hub/*.json) as reference data
rules.rationale: Historical data is static and available to all teams safely

rules.rule: The coordinator is the ONLY entity that merges cross-project data
rules.rationale: Prevents race conditions in consolidation. Commander has full visibility.

rules.rule: Newest data takes priority over older data
rules.rationale: Per SOP-015 data priority rules. Current test results > old reports.

section_4_findings_taxonomy.title: Standard Findings Taxonomy
section_4_findings_taxonomy.description: Consistent categorization for all findings across all teams.

categories.bug: Code defect that causes incorrect behavior
categories.race_condition: Concurrency bug that manifests under parallel access
categories.resource_leak: File handles, connections, or memory not properly released
categories.missing_validation: Input not checked, allowing invalid state
categories.performance: Inefficiency that degrades speed or resource usage
categories.test_gap: Missing test coverage for a feature or edge case
categories.design: Architectural issue or suboptimal design pattern
categories.redundancy: Duplicated code or functionality across modules

severity_levels.critical: Must fix immediately. System fails or produces wrong results under normal use.
severity_levels.high: Fix soon. Manifests under concurrent use or specific conditions.
severity_levels.medium: Fix when convenient. Edge case or minor degradation.
severity_levels.low: Nice to fix. Cosmetic, documentation, or minor improvement.

quick_reference.consolidation_command: python3 -c "import json,glob; files=glob.glob('storage/coordination/hub/infrastructure-*.json'); [print(f'{f}: {json.load(open(f))["metadata"]["team"]} - {json.load(open(f))["metadata"]["task"]}') for f in sorted(files)]"
quick_reference.data_flow_summary: Teams write to isolated outputs → Commander collects → Validates → Deduplicates → Cross-references → Assembles master report
quick_reference.key_principle: Data flows UP to the commander, never sideways between project groups

procedures: All team outputs must include standard metadata block (team, task, date, project_group, etc.)
Follow report_types schema for index, bug, documentation, and assessment reports
Run 6-step consolidation pipeline: collect, validate, categorize, deduplicate, cross-reference, assemble
Apply 5 data flow rules (DF-01 through DF-05) for inter-team data sharing
Use standard findings taxonomy categories and severity levels for consistent reporting
